chunks: And from him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The nobility of the believer is the night prayer, and the honor of the believer is restraining himself from the faults of people."

key_terms.أَعْرَاضِ النَّاسِ: Faults or private matters of people

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of a true believer's nobility and honor according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates night prayer (Salat al-Layl) as the distinctive mark of spiritual nobility, linking it to the Quranic concept of standing in prayer during the last third of the night. Simultaneously, it defines social honor (Izz) through 'Kaff al-Aradd', the act of restraining oneself from scrutinizing or exposing the private faults of others, thereby fostering communal dignity.
